editions.text:
The station logged 25 species and 141 feeder visits, a quieter day than the previous week's average of 19.4 species and 257.3 visits. Regulars such as the Tufted Titmice, Carolina Chickadees, and Northern Cardinals held steady. The Eastern Bluebird was back after 11 days away, with the previous record dated September 27. No new species were first heard or seen at the station, and no first confident visual records were established.

Visual activity began with the Eastern Towhee 16 minutes before sunrise and concluded with the Northern Cardinal 1 minute after sunset. The Rose-breasted Grosbeak was seen perching on a black metal feeder stand, while a Tufted Titmouse was observed feeding on seeds at a suet cage feeder.
